def transform(grid):
    g = np.array(grid)
    bg = background(g)
    comps = components(g == bg)
    big = max(comps, key=len)
    y0, x0, y1, x1 = bbox(big)
    # peel edges that are mostly not the rectangle colour
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        if (g[y0, x0:x1+1] == bg).mean() < 0.5:
            y0 += 1; changed = True
        if (g[y1, x0:x1+1] == bg).mean() < 0.5:
            y1 -= 1; changed = True
        if (g[y0:y1+1, x0] == bg).mean() < 0.5:
            x0 += 1; changed = True
        if (g[y0:y1+1, x1] == bg).mean() < 0.5:
            x1 -= 1; changed = True
    rect = crop(g, y0, x0, y1, x1)
    out = rect.copy()
    emit(out, "Crop the large solid rectangle, including the few odd-coloured dots inside it.")
    dots = [(y, x) for y in range(rect.shape[0]) for x in range(rect.shape[1]) if rect[y, x] != bg]
    for (y, x) in dots:
        c = rect[y, x]
        out[y, :] = c
        out[:, x] = c
        emit(out, f"Extend the dot at ({y},{x}) into a full row and column of colour {c}.")
    emit(out, "Final grid: the rectangle with every dot's row and column filled.")
    return out
